sections.text:
Once upon a time, in a beautiful and quiet town, there lived a gentle and kind girl named Cinderella.

Cinderella had a very happy life with her loving parents, where things were going well.

But fate had great sadness in store for her when her mother fell ill and died while she was still young.

The father was very sad to part with his wife, but he decided to marry again to compensate his daughter for the lost tenderness of her mother.

The father married a woman who appeared elegant and respectable, and she had two daughters who were approximately the same age as Cinderella, Anastasia and Drizella.

At first, Cinderella's stepmother treated Cinderella kindly in front of her father, but things changed completely once her father died during one of his business trips.

The stepmother showed her true cruel face and began treating Cinderella like a servant in her own household.

The stepmother stripped Cinderella of her beautiful clothes and warm room, and placed her in a cold, small room in the attic.

Cinderella was forced to do all the hard housework from dawn until late at night.

She was sweeping, mopping, washing clothes, and cooking food for her stepmother and her two spoiled daughters, who did nothing but make fun of her.

Despite all this fatigue and cruelty, Cinderella maintained her kindness and inner purity, and she used to sing to the birds and talk to the house mice, who became her loyal friends.

One day, the king's palace announced the holding of a large and dancing party, to which all the single girls in the kingdom were invited.

The goal of this ceremony was for the young prince to choose a bride for himself from among the girls of the kingdom.

Joy spread throughout the house, and the stepmother and her two daughters began preparing for this great event by buying luxurious dresses and precious jewelry.

Cinderella asked sheepishly if she could come, and the stepmother laughed and said, “You? With those torn clothes of yours? You will only go if you finish all the housework and patch up an old dress.”

Cinderella worked hard all day to finish her chores, and with the help of her friends, the mice and birds, she was able to sew an old dress for her mother and make it look beautiful.

But when the stepmother's two daughters saw the dress, they became extremely jealous and brutally tore it until they destroyed it completely.

Cinderella cried bitterly and went into the garden of the house, where she felt complete despair for the first time.

Suddenly, bright lights appeared in the garden, and a kind-faced woman holding a magic wand appeared in front of her; She's the good fairy godmother!
The fairy said with a smile: “Don’t cry, my little one. You are a good girl and you deserve to go to the ball.”

With a quick movement of her wand, the fairy transformed a large gourd into a magnificent golden carriage, four mice into purebred white horses, and a horse and a dog into the coachman and guard of the carriage.

Finally, the fairy touched Cinderella's torn dress, and in seconds it turned into a stunning spherical dress that shone like the stars in the sky, along with a thin, transparent glass shoe, the likes of which had never been made.

Before Cinderella got into the carriage, the fairy warned her sternly: “Remember, my daughter, the magic will be broken when the clock strikes midnight, so be sure to leave before that.”

Cinderella arrived at the palace, and as soon as she entered the ballroom, the music stopped and all eyes turned to her because of her enchanting beauty.

Even her stepmother and two daughters did not recognize her and thought she was a princess from a distant land.

The young prince immediately came forward and asked her to dance, and they danced together all evening, never taking his eyes off her for a moment.

Cinderella felt so happy that she completely forgot the time, until she heard the chimes of the palace clock announcing the approach of midnight: strike.

Knock.

Cinderella remembered the fairy's warning, so she apologized to the prince and ran quickly towards the palace door.

The prince tried to catch up with her, shouting: "Wait! I don't know your name yet!", but she continued running up the long stairs.

In her haste, one of her glass slippers fell on the stairs, but she did not stop to pick it up because the magic was beginning to wear off.

Cinderella returned to her shabby clothes, and the glass slipper remained the only clue to the prince.

The next day, the prince decreed that the girl whose foot fit the glass slipper would be his wife.

Palace guards went around all the kingdom's houses, and hundreds of girls tried on the shoes, but they did not fit anyone.

The guards arrived at Cinderella's house, and Anastasia and Drizella tried to force their big feet into the small shoe, but to no avail.

The stepmother had locked Cinderella in the attic so that the guards would not see her, but the brave mice managed to steal the key and smuggle her out.

Cinderella appeared before the guards and asked to try on the shoe.

Her stepmother made fun of her, but the guard insisted on following the prince's order, and when Cinderella inserted her foot, the shoe fit her perfectly!
To confirm, Cinderella took the second one out of her pocket, much to the shock of her stepmother and two daughters.

Cinderella was taken to the palace, and the prince immediately recognized her despite her simple clothes, because her heart was what attracted him to her.

The prince married Cinderella in a legendary wedding, and thanks to her big heart, she forgave her stepmother and her two daughters, and lived happily and happily all her life.
